layerPolicy: unit + integration only (no live cluster layer this round)

premise.claim: The port allocator can hand the same randomly allocated port to different host-network pods, and nothing tells the scheduler, so two pods with the same port can be co-located on one node and the second process fails to bind.

tests.name: TestVerifyP0BasePremiseHostNetworkPodIsInvisibleToScheduler
tests.file: scripts/base_premise_test.go (copied into pkg/port-allocator/ on the base worktree)

tests.name: L2 base differential: test/envtest/testcase/portallocator suite copied onto base

premise.evidence: results/base-premise.txt (FAIL on base 7894133: scheduler-visible host ports empty), results/l2-envtest-base.txt (FAIL on base: 'host-network pod ... must declare hostPort 30012 for the scheduler')

findings.title: Injected pod specs must pass real kube-apiserver create-time validation
Re-injection of the same allocations is idempotent and stays API-valid
Upgrade gap: pods created before the controller change never declare hostPort, so NodePorts cannot protect them; docs do not state that the guarantee applies only to newly created pods

tests.name: TestVerifyCanaryLegacyPodWithoutDeclarationIsInvisibleToNodePorts
tests.note: canary: passes while the gap exists; invert/promote if declarations are ever backfilled or legacy pods recreated

findings.title: Full chain: RBG -> RoleInstanceSet (RoleScoped allocation) -> RoleInstance -> pod created through a real apiserver with containerPort == hostPort == allocated port
Non-host-network pods declare containerPort with hostPort == 0 (declarative, no node-port reservation)

liveNote: L3 (live cluster) not run this round: the spread-across-nodes contract needs a real kube-scheduler; the PR's own e2e test covers it and skips on <2 schedulable nodes. If run live, check: two host-network pods sharing a RoleScoped port land on different nodes (controller logs show both pods declaring the same hostPort).
